data.name: Aqeeq
data.gender_notes: Aqeeq is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Aqeeq is the name given to a feast held for the prophet Ibrahim on the seventh day after the birth of his son Ismail. This feast is commemorated in the Islamic tradition by sacrificing an animal or offering gold or silver as a symbolic act of obedience to Allah. The name Aqeeq carries the meaning “Feast” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Aqeeq usually hope their child will grow to embody feast and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aqeeq signifies the celebration of the birth of Prophet Ibrahim's son Ismail and the remembrance of Allah's blessings.
data.etymology: Aqeeq belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Feast.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aqeeq total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The Aqeeq feast is an important cultural tradition in many Islamic communities. It is a time to celebrate and give thanks for the birth of a new child, to gather with family and friends, and to strengon northern islamic bonds of love and unity.
data.spiritual_significance: The Aqeeq feast also holds deep spiritual significance in the Islamic tradition. It is a reminder of the great sacrifice and obedience of Prophet Ibrahim, who was willing to offer up his beloved son Ismail as a sacrifice to Allah. The act of sacrificing an animal, or making a monetary offering, symbolizes this obedience and submission to Allah's will, and the ongoing commitment to raise and care for a new child in accordance with Islamic values and teachings.
